# First writing session

Start with any of BrightHeart, Artificial Magi or Sing for the Dead, and one book or story you want to work on. Use the project-local source map, dossier and ledger views already prepared for that project. Carry forward choices the author has already made; do not ask for the same permission again. The author can write, dictate or bring an idea. The operator handles preparation and checks; the author does not need to run CLI commands or tests.

Before describing runtime work, make the prepared story memory easy to inspect. Follow the author's current project choice; an earlier document-delivery order does not restrict writing. Update each project's START-HERE and RESULTS with actual findings and current review status. Replace completed internal assignment notes. Distinguish source review, local document opening, software readiness and actual author acceptance; an interface issue must not hide completed dossiers or trigger another full reading.

Writing can begin in chat before completing the acceptance list. The author can brainstorm, dictate, develop passages and receive source-backed checks; new ledger entries remain provisional. Formal promotion and unmanaged-edit reconciliation currently require the author's direct answer at the terminal. Chat approval does not create that engine receipt, and the operator must not manufacture it. John's first acceptance sitting remains to be completed.

## Begin with a brief and a useful writing goal

Build a short brief: the selected work and passage or idea, what the author wants to achieve, the relevant current material, and any decision that would materially affect the next writing step. Use the current draft as the record of what is written. Treat the Bible as useful but fallible, and distinguish dated author intention from written events, proposals and older history. A newer author choice can supersede earlier guidance without silently rewriting the historical source.

Make the theme understandable in one plain English sentence, supported by concrete choices or consequences. Apply Elegance to both selecting and expressing it. New interpretations remain proposed working themes until author review; reuse established author choices. Identify the governing structure for the selected unit and the whole work or series, including relevant intermediate groups. Show how actual or proposed material serves that structure, rather than merely naming a framework. Follow [project onboarding](onboarding.md) for the fuller theme and structure guidance.

For a new idea, no Bible is required. Begin with brainstorming or a provisional premise, offer useful voice and structure options, and research a specific uncertainty when it matters to the writing. Do not require a complete plan before drafting can begin.

## Keep the first review bounded

Treat new material as a coherent writing unit: a proposed change, connected passage, scene or short story. Preserve the original draft or dictation transcript before interpretation. Compare the changed material with the relevant current passages and book/story dossier, adding series or collection context where an actual dependency requires it. Batch related changes within that unit; do not launch separate model calls for every fact or heading, restart onboarding, or reread the entire project by default.

Explain what fits, what changes an existing relationship or plan, and which thematic or structural consequences matter. Distinguish suggestions from the author's decisions. After review, use the existing scoped capture and acceptance paths to update the same project ledger and its readable views, retaining superseded material as history. New creative choices remain provisional until the author chooses them. If a check is slow or incomplete, preserve its input and evidence and diagnose the specific failure before another attempt.

The engine's first-session contract starts from that brief and narrows the review to at most **12 real choices** relevant to the sitting. Retain other matters for later. Present one question at a time, with enough story context to explain its consequence and a recommendation the author can assess. Group inseparable issues coherently; do not turn every source record or scene into a separate permission request. Provisional writing can continue around choices that do not block the selected task.

Then work on the chosen material. Explain useful continuity, thematic and structural implications at the affected levels, and distinguish an editorial suggestion from an accepted author decision. Keep the existing ledger and acceptance path; this guide does not introduce another workflow or store.

Operator readiness is not John's first acceptance sitting or W11 signoff. Those require the actual author session, its real choices and the agreed writing trial. Prepared dossiers, documentation and successful operator tests alone do not establish that outcome.

## Operator contract — formal 0037

- Optional project configuration `ledger_sources[]` explicitly selects initial source directories. When absent, the legacy recursive walk applies. When present, reject invalid or missing directory entries, overlapping roots and links escaping the allowed source boundaries.
- The `source_files` registry in the existing `commit.json` must retain newly scoped prose sidecars through acceptance. Default capture remains within the selected sources and must never automatically activate existing excluded legacy material.
- `source_relocations` explicitly maps an original receipt path prefix to a contained, currently selected copy. Do not infer a relocation or use it to admit material outside the selected sources.

The first-writing operator release has passed its recorded source, session and integration checks for all three projects. Actual trial inputs, source bytes, citations, served-family receipts and failed timing targets remain in the evidence. These checks do not prove John's author sitting. Use the existing engine surface and validated capabilities; this guide creates no new public verb or alternate session mechanism.
